content.title: About
content.content: Brandy and cola is a mix of classic brandy and carbonated cola, creating a refreshing, slightly sweet drink with the aroma of aged spirit. It is often served over ice as a cocktail.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brandy is produced by distilling wine, and its aging in oak barrels gives it a distinctive flavor.
The combination of brandy and cola is popular in the US and Europe as a light evening cocktail.
In some countries the drink is called “Brandy‑Cola” or “Brandy‑Cola Freeze”.
Cola is chosen for its sweetness, which softens the strength of the brandy.
A variant with lime or lemon adds an extra citrus note.

items.title: Antioxidants in brandy
items.content: Brandy contains polyphenols that may provide antioxidant effects.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine in cola and alcohol in brandy give a quick energy lift and a feeling of alertness.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Moderate alcohol can stimulate gastric juice secretion, aiding digestion.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Brandy contains about 35–40 % alcohol; excessive consumption can lead to intoxication.

items.title: Sugar in cola
items.content: High sugar content increases calories and may contribute to tooth decay and weight gain.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain drugs, so caution is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 30–50 ml of brandy into a glass with ice, add 150–200 ml of cola, stir gently. Optionally garnish with a lemon or lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Brandy should be kept in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. Cola should be refrigerated after opening to maintain carbonation.
